newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paribas cuts recommendation on GAN.
newsitem.headline: Paribas cuts recommendation on GAN.

text.p: Paribas Capital Markets said on Wednesday that it lowered its recommendation on the stock of state-controlled insurer Groupe des Assurances Generales (GAN) to no action from buy, citing a report that GAN may need 20 billion francs of refinancing prior to privatisation.
"We are surprised by the size of the latest estimates," published in the newspaper Le Monde, it said in a stock comment.

"If the article, though, is correct, anything left for shareholders is left completely at the whim of the state and will really depend upon the way in which GAN is valued by the privatisation commission -- the last valuation in 1995 was 270 francs a share.

"This is similar to the Credit Lyonnais situation. In that case, the state took over all Credit Lyonnais' bad loans and the minority shareholders got off lightly. GAN shareholders probably have less leverage than at Credit Lyonnais and we have no idea what the state would be prepared to leave them," it said.

"If the Le Monde article is on the right track we cannot continue to recommend the shares as a buy. The recent price flip up to 114 francs from 102 francs looks like a chance to make an orderly exit while the opportunity exists," it said.
GAN shares were down 0.89 percent at 111.30 francs at 1120 GMT.
